Definition: from G1443; a Hebræan (i.e. Hebrew) or Jew:--Hebrew.
BiblicalUsage: A Hebrew was an Israelite by birth and by tongue, and Paul claims the name with pride. In 2 Corinthians 11:22 he asks, are they Hebrews, so am I, in Philippians 3:5 he calls himself a Hebrew of the Hebrews, and in Acts 6:1 the Grecian widows are neglected in the daily ministration while the Hebrews are served.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the name is about belonging: Paul never stopped being a Hebrew when he became an apostle to the Gentiles, and the church had to learn that belonging to Christ does not erase where you came from. I hold that the church is wider than any one tongue or tribe, and the Hebrew of the Hebrews proves it.
